free_tier.stated: The cheapest large machine found: 4 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM, 50 GB system disk, 50 Mbps with a 1 TB monthly cap that falls to 10 Mbps once reached, at CNY 99 a year, quoted as 4C4G 50G 50Mps 99元/年. The vendor sells it as a student offer restricted to ages 18 to 25.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: If a user held a mainland identity and a filed domain, this is 4 cores and 4 GiB for the price of two coffees a year; without them it is unreachable, which is the whole finding.

limits.value: The 1 TB monthly transfer is the first thing to bind: past it the port drops to 10 Mbps rather than stopping, so a 500 GB day of transfer takes about 111 hours at the throttled rate. The student offer also carries no 24-hour refund.

notes: New to the corpus. Recorded as the floor of the Chinese annual market with its spec intact, because the number is what makes it interesting and the gates are what make it unusable for a user. CNY 99 a year is quoted as written and not converted. The 1 TB cap and the 10 Mbps throttle are the vendor's own words in the offer post, not a measurement.
